messages:
maya: Hey — noticed sustained allreduce latency spikes in euc1-gpu-pool after the infra patch last night :warning:
sam: Which patch? kernel/driver/firmware?
maya: The network stack push: switch fw + HBA driver bump. A subset of racks show throughput drop ~10x.
jia: I saw the alerts, digging logs now. Any pattern by rack or ToR?
noah: Quick grep shows a bunch of hosts with link speed falling back to 10Gbps on IB HCA side. Can't be right for 100G fabric.
ops-bot: Deploy bot: network-fw-rollout completed 03:12 UTC (canary 5 racks, then bulk).
maya: Here's a sample from one affected host:
```
$ ibv_devinfo -d mlx5_0
device: mlx5_0
  firmware: 13.25.1020
  node GUID: 0x1234...
  link_layer: InfiniBand
  phys_port_cnt: 2
  port 1:
    state: PORT_ACTIVE (4)
    max_mtu: 4096 (5)
    active_mtu: 4096 (5)
    gid_tbl_len: 128
    port_cap_flags: 0x02510a68
    max_msg_sz: 0x40000000
    active_speed: 10 Gb/sec (downshifted)
```
sam: Wow — active_speed 10 Gb/sec. That explains the allreduce slowdown. Does ethtool show the same on the NIC?
jia: ethtool on corresponding eth device shows 100Gbps advertised, but link negotiation ended up at 10G on the HCA. Looks like auto-neg fallback mismatch between ToR and HBA FW.
noah: This smells like the new ToR fw enabled stricter autoneg/LLDP heuristics and the mlx5 FW/driver misinterprets it -> drops to legacy negotiation.
maya: Agreed. Performance graph: collective bandwidth dropped right when the fw-rollout batch moved from canary to rack-12.
sam: Immediate mitigation: throttle the rollout. Can we pin affected racks to previous ToR firmware and force HCA to re-negotiate?
jia: Quick test commands I ran: 
```
# force re-neg and set port speed (temporary)
sudo ethtool -s eth0 speed 10000 autoneg off
# then bring down/up the device
sudo ip link set eth0 down && sudo ip link set eth0 up
```
That brought link back to 100G after re-probing on one host, but it's invasive and not scalable.
noah: We should avoid mass host reboots. Planned action: pause network-fw-rollout now, open rollback PR for ToR fw to v1.2.3 (previous), and run a per-rack audit script to detect downshifted HCAs.
maya: Can we also pin the mlx5 driver to previous version on a small canary pool? That might help isolate whether HBA driver interacts badly with new ToR changes.
sam: I'll make a short patch to our node image to pin driver and schedule a 5-host canary in euc1. Jia, can you prepare the audit script and a quick query to map allred jobs impacted?
jia: On it. I can run an ibv_devinfo grep across the fleet and produce a CSV. Also adding a check for active_speed != expected in our node-exporter metrics.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2025-0923 - IB link-downshift causing NCCL slowdowns. Assigned: sam, jia, noah.
noah: Timeline: pause rollout now, identify racks with downshift, revert ToR fw on affected racks, apply HBA driver pin on canary, validate allreduce bandwidth on canaries, then proceed with a revised rollout with autoneg toggles disabled on ToR side.
maya: FYI, some affected jobs can tolerate temporary fallback to smaller world sizes; I'll coordinate job retries with sched team to reduce tail impact.
sam: I'll post updates to this thread after the rollback PR and when canary validation completes. Thanks for quick triage everyone :thumbsup:
noah: +1 — will also notify our cloud partner about potential firmware regression.
maya: Thanks — keeping this thread open for status.
